review_notes: The file has a single theorem and no simp attributes of its own. I read the definitions and declarations it uses: reversedPath, reversedPath_zero, reversedPath_one, reversedFinitePhysicalPath and physicalTollCost_reversed. I also grepped for other uses of these lemmas across lean/OAI/Analysis/CircleDomains. The simp-interface concern is that the endpoint and cost lemmas for reversed paths are plain theorems with no @[simp] attribute. There is also no simp lemma for the val of reversedFinitePhysicalPath. Every caller has to unfold by hand with `change` and then use `rw`. I have not run Lean. I did not check whether the proposed simp lemmas would conflict with other simp sets, though reversedPath_zero and reversedPath_one look orientation-safe because the right-hand side is strictly smaller. I made no claim about loops or simp failures.

findings.problem: reversedPath_zero and reversedPath_one are plain theorems, not simp lemmas. There is also no simp lemma saying (reversedFinitePhysicalPath e y₀ γ).val = reversedPath γ.val; it holds only by rfl. Because of that, the proof cannot state hρ0, hρ1 and hρA with `simp`. Each one needs a manual `change` to expose `reversedPath γ.val ⊥`, followed by `rw`/`rwa`. The same four-line pattern is repeated in other files (AnchoredDustBlock, DistinctJunctionBlock, SingleDustJunction). Other files use `simpa only [reversedPath_zero]` instead, which shows the lemmas are the intended normal-form rewrites. The `change` steps depend on definitional unfolding, so they break if the definition is reorganised.
findings.proposed_change: In LastEntryCuts.lean, mark `reversedPath_zero : reversedPath γ ⊥ = γ ⊤` and `reversedPath_one : reversedPath γ ⊤ = γ ⊥` with `@[simp]`. Both are terminating and orientation-safe, since each right-hand side drops a `reversedPath`. In ReversedPhysicalOccupation.lean, add `@[simp] theorem reversedFinitePhysicalPath_val ... : (reversedFinitePhysicalPath e y₀ γ).val = reversedPath γ.val := rfl`. Then hρ0 and hρ1 can be proved by `simpa using hFO hend` and `simpa using hstart`. The `change`/`rw` steps in hρA can be replaced by `simp` calls. The same simplification applies to the other call sites.
findings.benefit: The reversed-path boilerplate in this proof and in at least three other files becomes a single `simp` call. The proofs no longer rely on defeq unfolding of reversedFinitePhysicalPath, so they are shorter and more robust to refactoring.

evidence.excerpt: theorem reversedPath_zero (γ : C(PathTime, X)) : reversedPath γ ⊥ = γ ⊤ := by

findings.problem: physicalTollCost_reversed states that the cost of the reversed path equals the cost of the original path. This is the natural simplification, since the right-hand side drops the reversal. It is not tagged @[simp], so each caller has to invoke it by name with `rw` or `exact`. The same manual use appears in SymmetricJumpEdges, AnchoredDustBlock, DistinctJunctionBlock and SingleDustJunction. Pairing it with the missing `reversedFinitePhysicalPath_val` simp lemma would let `simpa using hpay ρ ...` close the step.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `physicalTollCost_reversed` in ReversedPhysicalOccupation.lean. Its left-hand side is headed by `reversedFinitePhysicalPath` and the right-hand side removes it, so the rewrite terminates.
findings.benefit: Cost statements about reversed paths normalise automatically. The `rw ... at hp` step and the matching `exact`/`.trans` boilerplate in downstream files can become `simp`/`simpa`.
